title: Understanding intervals
summary: The distance between two notes is the building block of every chord and scale.

steps.title: What is an interval?
steps.body: An interval is the distance between two pitches, measured in semitones. The fretboard makes this physical: 1 fret = 1 semitone. Two notes 7 frets apart are a perfect 5th; two notes 4 frets apart are a major 3rd; the rest of theory is built on naming and combining these.

steps.title: Octave shapes
steps.body: The same note, 12 semitones apart. The most useful shape: skip a string and move 2 frets up (string 6 -> string 4). Use it to find any root note in a hurry.

steps.title: The big six
steps.body:
Memorize these by feel:
- m3 (3 semis) -- minor third, the 'sad' interval
- M3 (4 semis) -- major third, the 'happy' interval
- P4 (5 semis) -- perfect fourth, like 'Here Comes the Bride'
- P5 (7 semis) -- perfect fifth, like the Star Wars opening
- M6 (9 semis) -- major sixth, like NBC's chime
- m7 (10 semis) -- minor seventh, like the Star Trek theme.
